issues.item: Triggers: Feeling Happy: Feeling happy or relaxed
issues.explanation: 'Feeling happy or relaxed' as a trigger is not impossible, but in this profile it is the only broad internal-state trigger alongside trauma-linked cues (hearing related names, ambulances) and is weakly connected to the rest of the formulation. The other nodes emphasize intrusive war memories, negative self-appraisals, and avoidance; a relaxation trigger without any corresponding threat content or appraisals about letting guard down is clinically hard to anchor here.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Mirror Checking: keep checking mirrors
issues.explanation: 'Keep checking mirrors' is difficult to reconcile with the rest of the profile. Mirror checking usually implies appearance/body-focused concern or hypervigilant scanning for current danger, but this profile has no Threat items and the formulation isolates Threat from the active network. The remaining maladaptive strategies (avoiding sleep, revenge fantasies) fit trauma intrusions and appraisals, whereas mirror checking addresses a symptom theme not otherwise represented.

vignette: Khmer-born firefighter, Sophea, still remembers the explosion that shattered his world in the war-torn streets of Phnom Penh. It was a sound that would become forever etched in his mind - a deafening bang that left him stumbling through the rubble, desperate to escape the chaos. Even now, 40 years later, the mere mention of certain names or the wail of an ambulance siren can transport him back to that fateful day. The memories are so vivid, so real, that Sophea often feels like he's reliving the trauma all over again. As a firefighter, Sophea has grown accustomed to responding to emergency situations, but his experiences in the war zone have left him with a lingering sense of unease. He can't shake the feeling that danger lurks around every corner, waiting to pounce. To cope, he's developed a habit of constantly scanning his surroundings for signs of threat - a nervous tic that's become second nature to him. Whenever he hears an explosion or bang sound, he's instantly on high alert, his senses heightened as he frantically searches for the source of the noise. Sophea has also begun to avoid sleep, fearing that the darkness will bring with it unwanted memories of the past. He'll often find himself lying awake at night, his mind racing with thoughts of revenge against those responsible for the trauma he endured. These fantasies have become a twisted form of comfort, allowing him to momentarily escape the feelings of powerlessness that still plague him. As the memories continue to haunt him, Sophea can't help but feel like they belong to someone else - a stranger who's somehow taken up residence in his mind. He'll often find himself lost in thought, reliving the trauma as if it were happening all over again. It's a feeling that's both disorienting and terrifying, leaving him wondering if he'll ever be able to shake off the memories that continue to define him. Despite his best efforts, Sophea can't help but feel like he's to blame for what happened - that somehow, someway, he could have prevented the trauma from occurring. He compares himself unfavorably to others, convinced that they would have handled the situation differently. This self-doubt has left him feeling dehumanized, like an object rather than a person. As Sophea navigates his daily life as a firefighter, these feelings of inadequacy and guilt continue to simmer just below the surface. He's become increasingly withdrawn, avoiding social situations and struggling to connect with those around him. His wife has noticed the change in him, but Sophea can't bring himself to open up about the trauma he endured. It's only when the triggers come flooding back - the names, the ambulances, the explosion sounds - that Sophea is forced to confront the memories he's been trying so desperately to avoid. The memories overwhelm him, threatening to consume him whole. In those moments, he feels like he's losing his grip on reality, unsure of how much longer he can keep the darkness at bay. As the years go by, Sophea has come to realize that he can't outrun his past forever. He knows he needs help, but the thought of facing his demons head-on is a daunting prospect. For now, he's stuck in this endless cycle of avoidance and self-doubt, unsure of how to break free from the memories that continue to haunt him.
